newsitem.title: CAMEROON: New Cameroon bank rises from ashes of old bank.
newsitem.headline: New Cameroon bank rises from ashes of old bank.

text.p: Cameroon has created a new bank, the Banque Internationale du Cameroun pour l'Epargne et le Commerce (BICEC), from the collapsed Banque Internationale pour le Commerce et l'Industrie du Cameroun (BICIC).

A Finance Ministry statement dated March 15 said the state and the majority state-owned Credit Foncier du Cameroun development bank held the majority stake in the new bank, which would be privatised in two or three years.
The Banques Populaires de France group was providing technical assistance, it added.

A senior finance ministry official told Reuters the government also planned to cede viable parts of the Credit Agricole du Cameroon to a consortium including Cameroonian investors, the International Finance Corporation and Credit Commercial de France.
The new bank, likely to be called Commercial Bank of Cameroon, could take over certain assets of the failed Meridien BIAO-Cameroon, he added.

Cameroon's banking sector went into decline in the 1980s after the general economy collapsed. By 1987 most commercial banks were technically insolvent. It has since been trying to restructure the banking and financial sector.
